vectors.name: uuid
vectors.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Uuid has no shorthand tag, so it travels in the 0xF3 envelope over sixteen bytes

vectors.name: timestamp-millis
vectors.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Timestamp(Millis) over an i64 count travels in the 0xF3 envelope; Go reads it as time.Time and writes nanoseconds

vectors.name: timestamp-seconds
vectors.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Timestamp(Seconds) travels in the 0xF3 envelope; Go writes it back in nanoseconds and Node writes a Date back in milliseconds

vectors.name: timestamp-micros
vectors.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Timestamp(Micros) travels in the 0xF3 envelope; Go and Node write it back in nanoseconds

vectors.name: unknown-logical
vectors.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a logical id this build does not know is read and re-encoded unchanged (Rust, and Go through Tagged); a host builder with no value to carry it in refuses the leaf rather than dropping the annotation, which is what Node does today (#446 tracks a carrier)

malformed.name: timestamp-leap-second
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a leap second has no count since the epoch in any unit and is refused

malformed.name: envelope-over-shorthand
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: there is one encoding per value, so an envelope over a type with a shorthand tag is refused

malformed.name: envelope-id-zero
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: id 0 means no logical type and has no envelope

malformed.name: envelope-known-id-bad-param
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a known id with a parameter it cannot take is refused

malformed.name: envelope-uuid-wrong-length
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a Uuid is sixteen bytes

malformed.name: envelope-nested
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: the envelope carries a physical scalar, not another envelope

malformed.name: envelope-unknown-over-undefined
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: the envelope carries a physical scalar; Undefined has a shorthand tag and is refused

malformed.name: envelope-unknown-over-date
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: the envelope carries a physical scalar; Date has a shorthand tag and is refused

malformed.name: envelope-unknown-over-array
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: the envelope carries a physical scalar, not a container

malformed.name: leaf-0xf4
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: 0xF4 is reserved for a longer envelope and is refused

malformed.name: leaf-0xf4-with-payload
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: 0xF4 is reserved for a longer envelope and is refused

malformed.name: envelope-timestamp-nanos
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a logical type with a shorthand tag is written with it, so Timestamp in nanoseconds (unit 3) inside the envelope is refused; units 0 to 2 have no shorthand and are accepted

malformed.name: envelope-undefined
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Undefined (id 1) has the shorthand tag 0x01 and is refused inside the envelope

malformed.name: envelope-decimal
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Decimal (id 4) has the shorthand tag 0x14 and is refused inside the envelope

malformed.name: envelope-timestamp-bad-unit
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Timestamp takes a unit of 0 to 3 as its parameter; 4 is refused

malformed.name: envelope-timestamp-not-int
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Timestamp admits only an int as its physical value; text is refused

malformed.name: envelope-timestamp-out-of-range
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a timestamp count outside the representable range (here an i128 of seconds far past year 262143) is refused

malformed.name: envelope-uuid-over-text
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: Uuid admits only sixteen bytes as its physical value; text of that length is refused

malformed.name: envelope-truncated
malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: the envelope is id, parameter and a physical scalar; a parameter and payload cut off are refused

normalized.name: decimal-negative-zero
normalized.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: a decimal negative zero reads back as zero with its scale kept, and zero is always written without the sign

normalized.rule: Typed null (vitaminc#493): an absent value of a fixed-width type, padded to that type's leaf length so its sealed length matches a present value's. A frame is never sealed, so it reads as null and is written back as the plain null

ciphertext_malformed.name: ct-none
ciphertext_malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: CT_NONE (0x02) is retired because a None is a null leaf; it is never written and refused when read

ciphertext_malformed.name: ct-none-in-sequence
ciphertext_malformed.rule: ADR 0001 section 3: CT_NONE is refused wherever it appears

leaf_type_aad.rule: LeafTypeAad (ADR 0001 section 3): the context is PAE(domain, base, kind, id) under the vitaminc-context encoding, where PAE is a u64-le count then each element as a u64-le length and its bytes, and each element is itself a typed piece: a PAE of two parts, the u64-le-prefixed label vitaminc/context/value/v1 and the u64-le-prefixed type label then the payload. The domain is bytes/v1 over vitaminc/aead/leaf-type/v2; the base is utf8/v1 over the base string; the kind is u8-le/v1 over the physical kind byte (null 0, bool 1, int 2, float 3, text 4, bytes 5; a cross-language commitment, never renumbered); the id is u8-le/v1 over the logical id byte, 0 for no logical type. The parameter is not bound: two vectors with the same base, kind and id and different parameters have the same context.
